clue.text: French tea shops tacitly involved in unmentionable work

parts.note: the French word for tea is thé

indicators.note: involved in the sense of tangled or convoluted, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: French tea rooms are quietly mixed up in some shady business nobody talks about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles SHOPS TACITLY into SCOTTISH PLAY. Actors avoid saying the name Macbeth in a theatre for fear of bad luck, so the play is unmentionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre superstition forbids naming Macbeth, so the euphemism refers to a work one must not mention.

clue.text: Pivotal bit of Christening ritual performed in name only

indicators.note: the central letter, on which the word pivots
performed in the sense of worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A key moment in a baptism, carried out as a formality.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of CHRISTENING is T; 'performed' turns RITUAL into ITULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular head holds a position nominally, with no real power.

clue.text: Bird bone's bitten off at both ends

indicators.note: both outer letters of the bone are bitten away

parts.note: the femur is the thigh bone, with 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A bird's bone has been nibbled at each end.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first and last letters of FEMUR leaves EMU.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless Australian runner is a kind of bird.

clue.text: One training pet to catch adder, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: the pet surrounds the other letters, catching them

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet

indicators.note: skip the odd-placed letters and keep the even ones

explanation.surface: A trainer is teaching a pet cat to catch snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring the odds' keeps the second and fourth letters of ADDER, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the armed forces or police.

clue.text: Serve up dry plonk — after starting it'll provide you with energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

indicators.note: the plonk word is used after its start is taken off

parts.note: plonk is cheap wine

explanation.surface: An instruction to serve dry, cheap wine, which will give you a lift once you've begun.
explanation.walkthrough: Brut is the label for the driest champagne; plonk is British slang for cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a machine that turns flow into power, so it supplies energy.

clue.text: Richard's red gave green in this!

definitions.text: Richard's red gave green in this!

parts.words: Richard's red gave green in this!
parts.note: the rainbow mnemonic Richard Of York Gave Battle In Vain: Richard stands for red, gave for green, and in for this colour

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone named Richard's reddish colour turning green.
explanation.walkthrough: British children learn the rainbow colours as 'Richard Of York Gave Battle In Vain'; the word 'in' there is the sixth colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep blue-violet hue is the sixth colour of the rainbow sequence.

clue.text: Traditionalist nomadic Bedouin assuming the mantle of husband

indicators.note: assuming a mantle means putting it on, so the outer letters wrap round
the mantle is the outer covering, so only the outer letters of husband
nomadic means wandering, so the letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A conservative desert nomad takes on the role of husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assuming the mantle' wraps the outer letters of husband round the scrambled tribesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hidebound is rigidly conventional, a stickler for old ways.

clue.text: Sterile elastic masks — a Doctor's best friend?

indicators.note: the phrase masks the answer, covering it inside

explanation.surface: Sterile elastic face masks are a doctor's best friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Leela was a companion of the Fourth Doctor in the BBC science-fiction series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: In Doctor Who, the Time Lord's companions are his closest allies, and Leela was one.

clue.text: Every fourth of July Canadians make the same mess as their neighbours

indicators.note: take the fourth, eighth, twelfth letters and so on of the following words

parts.words: July Canadians make the same mess

explanation.surface: Every Fourth of July, Canadians are said to mess up just as much as Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth of July' looks like US Independence Day, but it tells you which letters to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans live south of Canada, so they are Canadians' neighbours.

clue.text: Report that goes with 11th subsidiary

parts.note: the ordinal suffix that goes with 11 to make '11th' is TH
subsidiary means lower or under

explanation.surface: A cryptic note about an eleventh-placed subsidiary report.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also works whole: thunder is what goes with lightning, the answer at 11-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, and the rumbling crash of a storm is one such noise.

clue.text: Resentment of first couple in club going for date

indicators.note: points to the opening pair of letters of the club word as the part to be swapped
one thing going for another means it replaces it

parts.note: a bludgeon is a heavy club

explanation.surface: Bitterness felt by the leading pair in a golf club when a date stands in.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth the dagger has gouts of blood 'on thy blade and dudgeon', dudgeon being the hilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to feel indignant anger, so the word names a feeling of offence.

clue.text: Inside of jacket keeps hot amid great burst of energy

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: the lining is the inner layer of a jacket

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the hot letter sits within the great letters

parts.note: GT is a standard abbreviation of great, as in Gt Britain
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A jacket's lining retains heat in the middle of a huge surge of power.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightning flash is a sudden electrical discharge, a burst of energy in a storm.

clue.text: To start with, grey parrot caught small lizard

indicators.note: says to take only the opening letter of the next word
caught as in heard, so the word is spelt by its sound

parts.note: to parrot is to echo, repeating someone's words

explanation.surface: First, a grey parrot snatched a little lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Geckos are small climbing lizards of warm countries.

clue.text: Pupil, feeding, asked for knife

indicators.note: the pupil is fed into the middle of the other word

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning asked or ordered
L is a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A schoolchild at lunch requests a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade is the cutting part of a knife, standing for the whole implement.

clue.text: Chalked up line in grass

indicators.note: the line word goes inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a cord is a line or string

explanation.surface: Someone scored a line on a pitch of grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To chalk something up is to register or note it, as a score is written on a board.

clue.text: Apex piece tops off river and wall crossings

indicators.note: the top letter of each crossing comes off

parts.note: a bridge is a river crossing (crossings serves both)
a stile is a set of steps for crossing a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A top piece caps off the places where you cross rivers and walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops off' drops the B of BRIDGE and the S of STILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge tile is a curved tile laid along the peak of a roof.

clue.text: Not clear? Write up its position in grid

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing up means the letters run bottom to top

parts.note: this entry sits in the middle of the grid, so its position is mid

explanation.surface: Unsure? Write up where it sits on the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim means faint or indistinct, so hard to make out.

clue.text: Signs given by a teacher cycling south

indicators.note: letters are cycled round, the last moving to the front

parts.note: a guru is a spiritual teacher
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A teacher bikes southwards, giving signals as she goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves GURU's final U to the front, giving UGUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens and portents are things that foretell the future, which is what augurs are.

clue.text: A French girl briefly stood up to strip on boat

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading the letters upwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A French girl rose briefly to take her clothes off on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens GIRL to GIR, and 'stood up' reverses it to RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a vessel is to strip it of its rigging, the ropes and sails.

clue.text: Emphatically hoping for children to change sides

indicators.note: right becomes left, so the R is swapped for an L

parts.note: broody describes someone longing to have a baby

explanation.surface: A would-be parent is so desperate for a baby they would defect.
explanation.definitionFit: As an intensifier, this swear word adds emphasis, so it works like 'very' or 'damn'.

clue.text: Singer, a bass, lifted title …

indicators.note: lifted means raised, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: a tenor is a singer
B stands for bass in music

explanation.surface: A singer and a bass stole a championship.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronetcy is a hereditary British rank, and its holder bears it as an honorific.

clue.text: One ending life of racehorse retired by the Queen

indicators.note: retired as in withdrawn, going backwards

parts.note: Red Rum was a famous racehorse, three times winner of the Grand National
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A racehorse put out to pasture by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's best-known steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer is someone who ends another's life.

clue.text: … plus points for winning teams

parts.note: up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up
sides are teams

explanation.surface: Following on from 19, bonus points for victorious teams.
explanation.definitionFit: Advantages or benefits are a situation's good aspects.

clue.text: Taking time, restored tattered screen

indicators.note: taking away the time letter from the fodder
tattered means torn to shreds, so the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Taking its time, someone restored a ragged screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T from RESTORED and 'tattered' rearranges RESORED into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Picture created from this one time in gentleman's address

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the time word sits inside the address

parts.note: Mr is how a gentleman is addressed
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A picture painted from a single moment in a man's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An imager is a device that forms images, so pictures come from it.

clue.text: Start trouser pockets

indicators.note: the word pockets the answer, holding it inside

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin putting things in your trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse someone is to wake or stir them, making them start up.

clue.text: Twist near end of knot to loosen

indicators.note: a twist near the end of the word moves one of its late letters round, swapping a pair

parts.note: to knot is to join, unite

explanation.surface: Twist the near end of a knot to loosen it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist near end of' swaps the I and T of UNITE, moving the I after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Undoing a knot frees whatever it held, so it loosens it.

clue.text: Relatively confused, Italy turns to English news provider

indicators.note: one thing turns into another, so the Italy letter is replaced

parts.note: messier means more confused, a comparative
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Getting comparatively muddled, the Italians switch to English for the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier carries tidings, so one who brings news is a news provider.

clue.text: Many questions asked of the newly professional?

definitions.meaning: papers of many questions set as tests
those newly turned professional are ex-amateurs

explanation.surface: Lots of questions put to people who have just turned pro.
explanation.definitionFit: Tests set in school or college consist of numerous questions.

clue.text: Nix Olympica's western extremity

definitions.meaning: nix is slang for zilch, not a thing
the leftmost letter of Olympica is O, which also stands for zero

explanation.surface: Nix Olympica is the old name of the Martian volcano Olympus Mons, and this sounds like its western edge.
explanation.definitionFit: O looks like zero, and zero means none at all, as does slang nix.

clue.text: Card game done naked finished outside

indicators.note: the finished word goes around the rest

parts.note: did means carried out or finished, as in 'I did the job'

indicators.note: naked means stripped of the outer layer, so the outer letters of game and done go

explanation.surface: A card game played in the nude ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' is the whole definition: a diamond is any card of that suit, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Any card of the suit of red lozenges is called by that suit's name.

clue.text: Metal in half-finished state

indicators.note: only half the word is done, so the first half

parts.note: Oregon is a US state

explanation.surface: Metal left in a half-completed condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is rock from which metal is extracted, so it stands loosely for metal.

clue.text: Twisted, withered women in theatre

indicators.note: twisted means contorted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: sisters are senior nurses on a hospital ward, women in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: Bent, wizened old women on stage: the witches of Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' turns WITHERED into THE WEIRD. Sister is the British title for a senior nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's three witches are gnarled crones who appear in a stage play.
